discovery: Discovery of spin-orbit torques: electrical switching of magnetization by in-plane currents via the spin Hall and interfacial spin-orbit effects
subfield: Condensed matter physics: spintronics and magnetism
motivation: Miron and Gambardella (Nature 2010, 2011) showed that an in-plane current through a heavy-metal/ferromagnet bilayer exerts a torque large enough to reverse a perpendicular magnet, with no second magnetic layer. Buhrman's group (Science 2012) identified the spin Hall effect in Pt and beta-tantalum as a quantitative source of this torque and demonstrated spin-Hall switching and oscillators. Together these results revealed that spin-orbit coupling converts charge current into a pure spin current that acts on magnetization. This turned a subtle relativistic transport effect into a general, robust way to write magnetic information. The discovery launched a field: spin-orbit torques have been reproduced in hundreds of laboratories and material systems, including antiferromagnets, topological insulators and 2D materials. They now underpin three-terminal SOT-MRAM, domain-wall and skyrmion motion, and terahertz antiferromagnetic dynamics. Its impact on fundamental spin physics and on technology is broad and lasting.
